title: Where early preachers preached, died, and were buried
english: Timothy, the bishop of Ephesus, was appointed by the blessed Paul. He came from the Gentiles, not from the circumcision, and Paul bears much witness to him, urging him to keep the good confession of the grace that had been given to him. In Ephesus he was gloriously martyred.
Titus was bishop of Crete. He preached the gospel of the Lord to the Cretans themselves and to the surrounding islands, and he died and was buried there.
Crescens preached the gospel of the Lord in Gaul, and there he is buried.

The eunuch of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ in Arabia Felix, on the island of Sri Lanka, and throughout the Red Sea region. The account has it that he too was gloriously martyred and buried there. His tomb remains an unconquerable weapon for the faithful against accursed barbarians, a refuge that drives away diseases and works healings even to this day.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Appendices ad indices apostolorum discipulorumque u01-open
orientation: The work opens by recording where several early Christian figures preached the gospel, died, and were buried, beginning with Timothy, bishop of Ephesus.
